_comment: The Accountability Ledger. Each entry is a concrete direction the Supreme Court issued to a government duty-bearer, with the granted period converted to an absolute 'due' date. Status is computed LIVE in the dashboard from 'due' vs today, EXCEPT where an explicit 'status' is set (missed/complied/ongoing) because a later tracked order confirms it. Every 'directive' is condensed from fetched order text — never invented. 'overdue'/'due-soon'/'upcoming' are never asserted as government failure; they mean the deadline has passed with compliance unconfirmed on the tracked record. Optional 'compliance_events': [{date, tid, note}] — dated facts from later orders about partial/progressive compliance (e.g. which States filed affidavits), rendered on the direction card without changing its status.

directions.directive: No heavy or commercial vehicle to park or stop on any National Highway carriageway or paved shoulder except at designated bays; enforced through ATMS real-time alerts, GPS-timestamped evidence and e-challans.
File a consolidated report on highway inspection teams, encroachments identified/demolished, and Rajmargyatra grievance-module operationalisation with toll-free 1033.
Demolish/remove all new or existing unauthorised dhabas, eateries and structures within the Right of Way of every National Highway.

No department, authority or local body shall grant or renew any licence, NOC or trade approval for a site within a Highway safety zone without prior NHAI/PWD clearance; all such existing licences shall be reviewed.
Constitute a District Highway Safety Task Force in every district the National Highway passes through, with the Collector and SP jointly responsible.

State Governments shall issue notifications prohibiting change of land use within 40 metres (residential) and 75 metres (commercial) of the mid-point of any National Highway, consistent with IRC norms; MoRTH to facilitate uniform notifications across all States in the same period.

Constitute dedicated Highway Surveillance Teams of State Police and Transport Department personnel for regular National Highway patrolling, supplementing NHAI's 24x7 route patrolling vehicles at intervals not exceeding 50 km, all fitted with Vehicle Tracking Devices.

Operationalise the Advanced Traffic Management System (cameras, speed detectors, message signs, emergency call boxes) across all 4/6-lane highways and file a compliance affidavit certifying each component.
Deploy BLS ambulances and recovery cranes at intervals not exceeding 75 km on every National Highway stretch (Article 21 positive duty of emergency response).
Publish a comprehensive list of accident blackspots on National Highways and issue a policy framework mandating high-mast lighting, speed cameras and reflective markings at each.

MoRTH shall place before the Court a report on the constitution of an Inter-State Highway Safety Coordination Committee to standardise enforcement protocols — uniform driving-hour limits, surveillance standards, parking enforcement and penalty regimes — across State boundaries.
File a consolidated district-wise and agency-wise compliance report before the Court on all of the above directions.
Conduct drone-based aerial highway surveys at least twice a year, with six-monthly reports filed before the Court.
Integrate all emergency/ambulance helplines (100, 101, 108, 102, 1033, 1091) into helpline 112, with concurrent mass-media publicity, and report compliance.
Establish functional physical and digital Good Samaritan Grievance Redressal Systems with State- and District-level nodal authorities.
Establish State Trauma Registries covering all medical facilities and link them to a Coordinated Trauma Registry (data format to be issued by MoHFW within 8 weeks).

Fully operationalise the PM RAHAT cashless-treatment scheme — designate hospitals, on-board the State Health Agency to the TMS, deploy police on eDAR — non-implementation declared a violation of the MV Act.
Constitute the National Road Safety Board under Section 215B of the Motor Vehicles Act (six months granted).
directions.status_note: 13 May 2026 order records the Board was not constituted; a final three-month extension was granted.

directions.directive: Constitute the National Road Safety Board — 'one last opportunity' after the 2025 deadline lapsed; NRSB Rules 2025 already framed.
Report compliance on clearing National Highway land of encroachments, with a toll-free complaint number and action-taken reports uploaded to a portal.
File an affidavit on the grievance-redressal machinery under the Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act 2002, with wide publicity of the mechanism.
Every State/UT to formulate and notify a State Road Safety Policy (deadline set at 31 Dec 2017); a foundational obligation the Court continues to monitor.
Every State/UT to establish a dedicated Lead Agency for road safety, licensing and vehicle standards (deadline set at 31 Dec 2017).
Every State/UT to constitute a dedicated Road Safety Fund; a standing obligation monitored order to order.
Incorporate road-safety education into the school curriculum of State Boards (deadline set at 1 Apr 2018).
Set up a permanent Road Safety Cell in the Ministry and in every State — the Court recorded these had been established and passed no further orders.
directions.status_note: 30 Nov 2017 order records the cells had been set up; no further orders sought on this direction.

directions.directive: Operationalise the hit-and-run compensation scheme under S.161 MV Act — Claims Enquiry Officer to forward a report within one month, compensation within 15 days of sanction, GIC to report annually; a standing scheme obligation the Court monitors.

Defaulting States and Union Territories shall file the compliance affidavits required by the 13 April 2026 directions within two weeks, failing which the Court will direct personal appearance (physical or virtual) of their Chief Secretaries/Administrators and Directors General of Police.
directions.status_note: Not complied with by the 27 July 2026 deadline: on 17 August 2026 the Court recorded that respondents who had not filed their affidavits shall still file them. Compliance then came in late — on 3 September 2026 the amicus curiae's chart showed every State/UT except Tamil Nadu had filed, with MoRTH and MHA also still in default. No Chief Secretary or DGP was ever summoned.

compliance_events.note: Court records compliance affidavits received from only 3 of 36 States/UTs — Bihar, Karnataka and Puducherry.
Court again directed respondents who have not filed affidavits to do so; matter listed for 1 September 2026.

Amicus curiae placed a compliance chart before the Court: all States, Union Territories and departments had by then filed affidavits except MoRTH, MHA and the State of Tamil Nadu — i.e. late compliance by every State/UT other than Tamil Nadu.
